types.name: Single rows
types.description: One line of plants per row at a fixed pitch, plants singulated along the row by a precision planter (corn, soybean in wide rows, cotton, sunflower, sugar beet). The row reader's default geometry.

types.name: Twin rows
types.description: Two lines of plants 18 to 24 cm apart on a wider centre (corn 7 to 8 in on 30 in centres, staggered along the row). From above at 2 cm or coarser the pair reads as one wide row; finer, it is two lines at a pitch that alternates short and long.

types.name: Skip rows
types.description: A regular pattern of planted and unplanted rows (cotton 2-and-1, seed-corn male rows cut out after pollination). The planted pitch and the pattern period differ; the reader sees the finer one and may report the coarser as an alternative.

types.name: Drilled
types.description: Narrow rows (12 to 25 cm) with plants not singulated along the row (small grains, drilled soybean). Rows resolve only while the canopy is open and at fine pixel sizes; plants do not.

types.name: Beds
types.description: Raised beds carrying one to three rows each, separated by furrows (furrow-irrigated corn and cotton in the US South, vegetables). The bed period is coarser than the row pitch.

types.name: Strip intercrop
types.description: Alternating strips of two crops a few rows wide (corn and soybean strips, maize-legume strips). Each strip has its own pitch; the field has two plantings.

types.name: Contour or terrace planting
types.description: Rows follow the land's contour lines, so they curve and change direction across the field. A row reader that fits straight lines per window still works if windows are small against the curvature.

types.name: Circular planting under a pivot
types.description: Rows planted in circles under a centre pivot (some LEPA systems). Locally straight, globally curved.

types.name: Tree lattice
types.description: Trees or vines at a fixed spacing along rows and across them (square, rectangular, offset, hedgerow). The planting-layout fitter's geometry.
